[BG 10.27] Know me to be Uchchaisravas among horses, brought forth by (the churning for) nectar, Airavata among princely elephants, and the king among men. [BG 10.28] Among weapons I am the thunderbolt, among cows I am (she called) Kamadhuk. I am Kandarpa the cause of reproduction, I am Vasuki among serpents. [BG 10.29] I am Ananta among Nagas, I am Varuna among aquatic beings, I am Aryaman among the Pitris, and Yama among those that judge and punish. [BG 10.30] I am Prahlada among the Daityas, and Time among things that count. I am the lion among the beasts, and Vinata's son among winged creatures. [BG 10.31] Of purifiers I am the wind. I am Rama among wielders of weapons. I am the Makara among fishes, and I am Jahnavi (Ganga) among streams. [BG 10.32] Of created things I am the beginning and the end and also the middle, O Arjuna. I am the knowledge of Supreme Spirit among all kinds of knowledge, and the disputation among disputants. [BG 10.33] Among all letters I am the letter A, and (the compound called) Dwanda among all compounds. I am also Time Eternal, and I am the Ordainer with face turned on every side. [BG 10.34] I am Death that seizeth all, and the source of all, that is to be. Among females, I am Fame, Fortune, Speech, Memory, Intelligence, Constancy, Forgiveness. [BG 10.35] Of the Sama hymns, I am the Vrihat-sama and Gayatri among metres. Of the months, I am Margasirsha, of the seasons (I am) that which is productive of flowers. [BG 10.36] I am the game of dice of them that cheat, and the splendour of those that are splendid. I am Victory, I am Exertion, I am the goodness of the good. [BG 10.37] I am Vasudeva among the Vrishnis, I am Dhananjaya among the sons of Pandu. I am even Vyasa among the ascetics, and Usanas among seers. [BG 10.38] I am the Rod of those that chastise, I am the Policy of those that seek victory. I am silence among those that are secret. I am the Knowledge of those that are possessed of Knowledge. [BG 10.39] That which is the Seed of all things, I am that, O Arjuna. There is nothing mobile or immobile, which can exist without me. [BG 10.40] There is no end, O chastiser of foes, of my divine perfections. This recital of the extent of (those) perfections hath been uttered by me by way (only) of instancing them. [BG 10.41] Whatever of exalted things (there is) or glorious, or strong, understand thou that everything is born of a portion of my energy. [BG 10.42] Or rather, what hast thou to do, by knowing all this in detail, O Arjuna? Supporting this entire universe with only a portion (of myself), I stand.

sections.title: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
sections.label: BG 11.1-8
sections.text: [BG 11.1] This discourse about the supreme mystery, called Adhyatman, which thou hast uttered for my welfare, hath dispelled my delusion. [BG 11.2] For I have heard at large from thee of the creation and dissolution of beings, O thou of eyes like lotus petals, and also of thy greatness that knoweth no deterioration. [BG 11.3] What thou hast said about thyself, O great Lord, is even so. O best of Male Beings, I desire to behold thy sovereign form. [BG 11.4] If, O Lord, thou thinkest that I am competent to behold that (form), then, O Lord of mystic power, show me thy eternal Self. [BG 11.5] Behold, O son of Pritha, my forms by hundreds and thousands, various, divine, diverse in hue and shape. [BG 11.6] Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Aswins, and the Maruts. Behold, O Bharata, innumerable marvels unseen before (by thee). [BG 11.7] Behold, O thou of curly hair, the entire universe of mobiles and immobiles, collected together in this body of mine, whatever else thou mayst wish to see. [BG 11.8] Thou art, however, not competent to behold me with this eye of thine. I give thee celestial sight. Behold my sovereign mystic nature.

sections.title: Sanjaya describes the universal form
sections.label: BG 11.9-14
sections.text: [BG 11.9] Having said this, O monarch, Hari, the mighty Lord of mystic power, then revealed to the son of Pritha his Supreme sovereign form, [BG 11.10] with many mouths and eyes, many wonderous aspects, many celestial ornaments, many celestial weapons uplifted, [BG 11.11] wearing celestial garlands and robes, (and) with unguents of celestial fragrance, full of every wonder, resplendent, infinite, with faces turned on all sides. [BG 11.12] If the splendour of a thousand suns were to burst forth at once in the sky, (then) that would be like the splendour of that Mighty One. [BG 11.13] The son of Pandu then beheld there in the body of that God of gods the entire universe divided and sub-divided into many parts, all collected together. [BG 11.14] Then Dhananjaya, filled with amazement, (and) with hair standing on end, bowing with (his) head, with joined hands addressed the God.

sections.title: Arjuna's vision: awe and terror
sections.label: BG 11.15-31
sections.text: [BG 11.15] I behold all the gods, O God, as also all the varied hosts of creatures, (and) Brahman seated on (his) lotus seat, and all the Rishis and the celestial snakes. [BG 11.16] I behold Thee with innumerable arms, stomachs, mouths, (and) eyes, on every side, O thou of infinite forms. Neither end nor middle, nor also beginning of thine do I behold, O Lord of the universe, O thou of universal form. [BG 11.17] Bearing (thy) diadem, mace, and discus, a mass of energy, glowing on all sides, do I behold thee that art hard to look at, endued on all sides with the effulgence of the blazing fire or the Sun, (and) immeasurable. [BG 11.18] Thou art indestructible, (and) the Supreme object of this universe. Thou art without decay, the guardian of eternal virtue. I regard thee to be the eternal (male) Being. [BG 11.19] I behold thee to be without beginning, mean, end, to be of infinite prowess, of innumerable arms, having the Sun and the Moon for thy eyes, the blazing fire for thy mouth, and heating this universe with energy of thy own. [BG 11.20] For the space betwixt heaven and earth is pervaded by Thee alone, as also all the points of the horizon. At sight of this marvellous and fierce form of thine, O Supreme Soul, the triple world trembleth. [BG 11.21] For these hosts of gods are entering thee. Some, afraid, are praying with joined hands. Saying Hail to Thee—the hosts of great Rishis and Siddhas praise Thee with copious hymns of praise. [BG 11.22] The Rudras, the Adityas, the Vasus, they that (called) the Siddhas, the Viswas, the Aswins, the Maruts, also the Ushmapas, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Asuras, the hosts of Siddhyas, behold Thee and are all amazed. [BG 11.23] Beholding Thy mighty form with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed one, with innumerable arms, thighs and feet, many stomachs, (and) terrible in consequence of many tusks, all creatures are frightened and I also. [BG 11.24] Indeed, touching the very skies, of blazing radiance, many-hued, mouth wide-open, with eyes that are blazing and large, beholding thee, O Vishnu, with (my) inner soul trembling (in fright), I can no longer command courage and peace of mind. [BG 11.25] Beholding thy mouths that are terrible in consequence of (their) tusks, and that are fierce (as the all-destroying fire at the end of the Yuga), I cannot recognise the points of the horizon nor can I command peace of mind. [BG 11.26] Be gracious, O God of gods, O thou that art the refuge of the Universe. And all these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with the hosts of kings, and Bhishma, and Drona, and also this Suta's son (Karna), [BG 11.27] accompanied by even the principal warriors of our side, are quickly entering thy terrible mouths rendered fierce by thy tusks. Some, with their heads crushed, are seen striking at the interstices of (thy) teeth. [BG 11.28] As many currents of water flowing through different channels roll rapidly towards the ocean, so these heroes of the world of men enter thy mouths that flame all around. [BG 11.29] As moths with increasing speed rush for (their own) destruction to the blazing fire, so also do (these) people, with unceasing speed, enter thy mouths for (their) destruction. [BG 11.30] Swallowing all these men from every side, thou lickest them with thy flaming mouths. Filling the whole universe with (thy) energy, thy fierce splendours, O Vishnu, are heating (everything). Tell me who thou art of (such) fierce form. [BG 11.31] I bow to thee, O chief of the gods, be gracious to me. I desire to know thee that art the Primeval One, I do not understand thy action.

sections.title: I am Time, the destroyer: be my instrument
sections.label: BG 11.32-34
sections.text: [BG 11.32] I am Death, the destroyer of the worlds, fully developed. I am now engaged in slaying the race of men. Without thee all these warriors standing in the different divisions shall cease to be. [BG 11.33] Wherefore, arise, gain glory, (and) vanquishing the foe, enjoy (this) swelling kingdom. By me have all these been already slain. Be only (my) instrument. O thou that can'st draw the bow with (even) the left hand. [BG 11.34] Drona and Bhishma, and Jayadratha, and Karna, and also other heroic warriors, (already) slain by me, do thou slay. Be not dismayed, fight; thou shalt conquer in battle (thy) foes.

sections.title: Arjuna's hymn and plea for forgiveness
sections.label: BG 11.35-46
sections.text: [BG 11.35] Hearing these words of Kesava, the diadem-decked (Arjuna), trembling, (and) with joined hands, bowed (unto him); and once more said unto Krishna, with voice choked up and overwhelmed with fear, and making his salutations (to him). [BG 11.36] It is meet, Hrishikesa, that the universe is delighted and charmed in uttering thy praise, and the Rakshasas flee in fear in all directions, and the hosts of the Siddhas bow down (to thee). [BG 11.37] And why should they not bow down to thee, O Supreme Soul, that are greater than even Brahman (himself), and the primal cause? O thou that art Infinite, O God of the gods, O thou that art the refuge of the universe, thou art indestructible, thou art that which is, and that which is not and that which is beyond (both). [BG 11.38] Thou art the First God, the ancient (male) Being, thou art the Supreme refuge of this universe. Thou art the Knower, thou art the Object to be known, thou art the highest abode. By thee is pervaded this universe, O thou of infinite form. [BG 11.39] Thou art Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, Moon, Prajapati, and Grandsire. Obeisance be to thee a thousand times, and again and yet again obeisance to thee. Obeisance to thee in front, and also from behind. [BG 11.40] Let obeisance be to thee from every side, O thou that art all. Thou art all, of energy that is infinite, and prowess that is immeasurable. Thou embracest the All. [BG 11.41] Regarding (thee) a friend whatever hath been said by me carelessly, such as—"O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend,"—not knowing this thy greatness from want of judgement or from love either, whatever disrespect hath been shown thee for purpose of mirth, on occasions of play, lying, sitting, (or) at meals, while alone or in the presence of others, O undeteriorating one, I beg thy pardon for it, that art immeasurable. [BG 11.42] Thou art the father of this universe of mobiles and immobiles. Thou art the great master deserving of worship. There is none equal to thee, how can there be one greater? [BG 11.43] O thou whose power is unparalleled in even three worlds? Therefore bowing (to thee) prostrating (my) body, I ask thy grace, O Lord, O adorable one. [BG 11.44] It behoveth thee, O God, to bear (my faults) as a father (his) son's, a friend (his) friend's, a lover (his) loved one's. [BG 11.45] Beholding (thy) form (unseen) before, I have been joyful, (yet) my mind hath been troubled, with fear. Show me that (other ordinary) form, O God. Be gracious, O Lord of the gods, O thou that art the refuge of the universe. [BG 11.46] (Decked) in diadem, and (armed) with mace, discus in hand, as before, I desire to behold thee. Be of that same four-armed form, O thou of a thousand arms, thou of universal form.

sections.title: The gentle form; only devotion reveals Krishna
sections.label: BG 11.47-55
sections.text: [BG 11.47] Pleased with thee, O Arjuna, I have, by my (own) mystic power, shown thee this supreme form, full of glory, Universal, Infinite, Primeval, which hath been seen before by none save thee. [BG 11.48] Except by thee alone, hero of Kuru's race, I cannot be seen in this form in the world of men by any one else, (aided) even by the study of the Vedas and of sacrifices, by gifts, by actions, (or) by the severest austerities. [BG 11.49] Let no fear be thine, nor perplexity of mind at seeing this awful form of mine. Freed from fear with a joyful heart, thou again see Me assuming that other form. [BG 11.50] Vasudeva, having said all this to Arjuna, once more showed (him) his own (ordinary) form, and that High-Souled one, assuming once more (his) gentle form, comforted him who had been afflicted. [BG 11.51] Beholding this gentle human form of thine, O Janardana, I have now become of right mind and have come to my normal state. [BG 11.52] This form of mine which thou hast seen is difficult of being seen. Even the gods are always desirous of becoming spectators of this (my) form. [BG 11.53] Not by the Vedas, nor by austerities, nor by gifts, nor by sacrifices, can I be seen in this form of mine which thou hast seen. [BG 11.54] By reverence, however, that is exclusive (in its objects), O Arjuna, I can in this form be known, seen truly, and attained to, O chastiser of foes. [BG 11.55] He who doth everything for me, who hath me for his supreme object, who is freed from attachment, who is without enmity towards all beings, even he, O Arjuna, cometh to me.

sections.title: The personal and the unmanifest
sections.label: BG 12.1-7
sections.text: [BG 12.1] Of those worshippers who, constantly devoted, adore thee, and those who (meditate) on thee as the Immutable and Unmanifest, who are best acquainted with devotion? [BG 12.2] Fixing (their) mind on me, they that constantly adore me, being endued (besides) with the highest faith, are deemed by me to be the most devoted. [BG 12.3] They, however, who worship the Immutable, the Unmanifest, the All-pervading, the Inconceivable, the Indifferent, the Immutable, the Eternal, who, restraining the entire group of the senses, [BG 12.4] are equal-minded in respect of all around and are engaged in the good of all creatures, (also) attain to me. [BG 12.5] The trouble is the greater for those whose minds are fixed on the Unmanifest; for the path to the Unmanifest is hard to find by those that are embodied. [BG 12.6] They (again) who, reposing all action on me (and) regarding me as their highest object (of attainment), worship me, meditating on me with devotion undirected to anything else, [BG 12.7] of them whose minds are (thus) fixed on me, I, without delay, become the deliverer from the ocean of (this) mortal world.

sections.title: A ladder of spiritual practices
sections.label: BG 12.8-12
sections.text: [BG 12.8] Fix thy heart on me alone, place thy understanding on me, Hereafter then shalt thou dwell in me. (There is) no doubt (in this). [BG 12.9] If however, thou art unable to fix thy heart steadily on me, then, O Dhananjaya, strive to obtain me by devotion (arising) from continuous application. [BG 12.10] If thou beest unequal to even (this) continuous application, then let actions performed for me be thy highest aim. Even performing all thy acts for my sake, thou wilt obtain perfection. [BG 12.11] If even this thou art unable to do, then resorting to devotion in me, (and) subduing thy soul, abandon the fruit of all actions. [BG 12.12] Knowledge is superior to application (in devotion); meditation is better than knowledge; the abandonment of the fruit of reaction (is better) than meditation; and tranquillity (results) immediately from abandonment.

sections.title: The qualities of a devotee dear to Krishna
sections.label: BG 12.13-20
sections.text: [BG 12.13] He who hath no hatred for any creature, who is friendly and compassionate also, who is free from egoism, who hath no vanity, attachment, who is alike in pleasure and pain, [BG 12.14] who is forgiving, contented, always devoted, of subdued soul, firm of purpose, with heart and understanding fixed on me, even he is dear to me. [BG 12.15] He through whom the world is not troubled, (and) who is not troubled by the world, who is free from joy, wrath, fear and anxieties, even he is dear to me. [BG 12.16] That devotee of mine who is unconcerned, pure, diligent, unconnected (with worldly objects), and free from distress (of mind), and who renounceth every action (for fruit), even he is dear to me. [BG 12.17] He who hath no joy, no aversion, who neither grieveth nor desireth, who renounceth both good and evil, (and) who is full of faith in me, even he is dear to me. [BG 12.18] He who is alike to friend and foe, as also in honour and dishonour, who is alike in cold and heat, (and pleasure and pain), who is free from attachment, [BG 12.19] to whom censure and praise are equal, who is taciturn, who is contented with anything that cometh (to him), who is homeless, of steady mind and full of faith, even that man is dear to me. [BG 12.20] They who resort to this righteousness (leading to) immortality which hath been (already) declared,—those devotees full of faith and regarding me as the highest object (of their acquisition) are the dearest to me.

sections.title: The field and the knower of the field
sections.label: BG 13.1-6
sections.text: [BG 13.1] This body, O son of Kunti, is called Kshetra. Him who knoweth it, the learned call Kshetrajna. [BG 13.2] Know me, O Bharata, to be Kshetras. The knowledge of Kshetra and Kshetrajna I regard to be (true) knowledge. [BG 13.3] What that Kshetra (is), and what (it is) like, and what changes it undergoes, and whence (it comes), what is he (viz., Kshetrajna), and what his powers are, hear from me in brief. [BG 13.4] All this hath in many ways been sung separately, by Rishis in various verses, in well-settled texts fraught with reason and giving indications of Brahman. [BG 13.5] The great elements, egoism, intellect, the unmanifest (viz., Prakriti), also the ten senses, the one (manas), the five objects of sense, desire, aversion, [BG 13.6] pleasure, pain, body consciousness, courage,—all this in brief hath been declared to be Kshetra in its modified form.

sections.title: The virtues that are true knowledge
sections.label: BG 13.7-11
sections.text: [BG 13.7] Absence of vanity, absence of ostentation, abstention from injury, forgiveness, uprightness, devotion to preceptor, purity, constancy, [BG 13.8] self-restraint, indifference to objects of sense, absence of egoism, perception of the misery and evil of birth, death, decrepitude and disease, freedom from attachment, [BG 13.9] absence of sympathy for son, wife, home, and the rest, and constant equanimity of heart on attainment of good and evil, [BG 13.10] unswerving devotion to me without meditation on anything else, frequenting of lonely places, distaste for concourse of men, constancy in the knowledge of the relation of the individual self to the supreme, [BG 13.11] perception of the object of the knowledge of truth,—all this is called Knowledge; all that which is contrary to this is Ignorance.

sections.title: The knowable: the supreme Brahman
sections.label: BG 13.12-18
sections.text: [BG 13.12] That which is the object of knowledge I will (now) declare (to thee), knowing which one obtaineth immortality. [BG 13.13] It is the Supreme Brahma having no beginning, who is said to be neither existent nor non-existent; whose hands and feet are on all sides, [BG 13.14] whose eyes, heads and faces are on all sides, who dwells pervading everything in the world, who is possessed of all the qualities of the senses (though) devoid of the senses, [BG 13.15] without attachment (yet) sustaining all things, without attributes (yet) enjoying (a) all attributes, without and within all creatures, immobile and mobile, not knowable because of (his) subtlety, remote yet near, [BG 13.16] undistributed in all beings, (yet) remaining as if distributed, who is the sustainer of (all) beings, the absorber and the creator (of all); who is the light of all luminous bodies, [BG 13.17] who is said to be beyond all darkness; who is knowledge, the Object of knowledge, the End of knowledge and seated in the hearts of all. [BG 13.18] Thus Kshetra, and Knowledge, and the Object of Knowledge, have been declared (to thee) in brief. My devotee, knowing (all) this, becomes one in spirit with me.

sections.title: Prakriti and Purusha: matter and spirit
sections.label: BG 13.19-34
sections.text: [BG 13.19] Know that Nature and Spirit are both without beginning (and) know (also) that all modifications and all qualities spring from Nature. [BG 13.20] Nature is said to be the source of the capacity of enjoying pleasures and pains. [BG 13.21] For Spirit, dwelling in nature enjoyeth the qualities born of Nature. The cause of its births in good or evil wombs is (its) connection with the qualities. [BG 13.22] The Supreme Purusha in this body is said to be surveyor, approver, supporter, enjoyer, the mighty lord, and also the Supreme Soul. [BG 13.23] He who thus knows Spirit, and Nature, with the qualities, in whatever state he may be, is never born again. [BG 13.24] Some by meditation behold the self in the self by the self; others by devotion according to the Sankhya system; and others (again), by devotion through works. [BG 13.25] Others yet not knowing this, worship, hearing of it from others. Even these, devoted to what is heard, cross over death. [BG 13.26] Whatever entity, immobile or mobile, cometh into existence, know that, O bull of Bharata's race, to be from the connection of Kshetra and Kshetrajna (matter and spirit). [BG 13.27] He seeth the Supreme Lord dwelling alike in all beings, the Imperishable in the Perishable. [BG 13.28] For seeing the Lord dwelling alike everywhere, one doth not destroy himself by himself, and then reacheth the highest goal. [BG 13.29] He seeth (truly) who seeth all actions to be wrought by nature alone in every way and the self likewise to be not the doer. [BG 13.30] When one seeth the diversity of entities as existing in one, and the issue (everything) from that (One), then is one said to attain to Brahma. [BG 13.31] This inexhaustible Supreme Self, O son of Kunti, being without beginning and without attributes, doth not act, nor is stained even when stationed in the body. [BG 13.32] As space, which is ubiquitous, is never, in consequence of its subtlety tainted, so the soul, stationed in every body, is never tainted. [BG 13.33] As the single Sun lights up the entire world, so the Spirit, O Bharata, lights up the entire (sphere of) matters. [BG 13.34] They that, by the eye of knowledge, know the distinction between matter and spirit, and the deliverance from the nature of all entities, attain to the Supreme.

sections.title: Krishna, the father of all beings
sections.label: BG 14.1-4
sections.text: [BG 14.1] I will again declare (to thee) that supernal science of sciences, that excellent science, knowing which all the munis have attained to the highest perfection from (the fetters of) this body. [BG 14.2] Resorting to this science, and attaining to my nature, they are not reborn even on (the occasion of) a (new) creation and are not disturbed at the universal dissolution. [BG 14.3] The mighty Brahma is a womb for me. Therein I place the (living) germ. Thence, O Bharata, the birth of all beings taketh place. [BG 14.4] Whatever (bodily) forms, O son of Kunti, are born in all wombs, of them Brahma is the mighty womb, (and) I the seed-imparting Sire.

sections.title: How sattva, rajas and tamas bind
sections.label: BG 14.5-18
sections.text: [BG 14.5] Goodness, passion, darkness, these qualities, born of nature, bind down, O thou of mighty arms, the eternal embodied soul in the body. [BG 14.6] Amongst these, Goodness, from its unsullied nature, being enlightening and free from misery, bindeth (the soul), O sinless one, with the attainment of happiness and of knowledge. [BG 14.7] Know that passion, having desire for its essence, is born of thirst and attachment. That, O son of Kunti, bindeth the embodied (soul) by the attachment of work. [BG 14.8] Darkness, however, know, is born of ignorance, (and) bewilders all embodied soul. That bindeth, O Bharata, by error, indolence, and sleep. [BG 14.9] Goodness uniteth (the soul) with pleasure; Passion, O Bharata, uniteth with work; but darkness, veiling knowledge, uniteth with error. [BG 14.10] Passion and darkness, being repressed, Goodness remaineth, O Bharata. Passion and goodness (being repressed), darkness (remaineth); (and) darkness and goodness (being repressed), passion (remaineth). [BG 14.11] When in this body, in all its gates, the light of knowledge is produced, then should one know that goodness hath been developed there. [BG 14.12] Avarice, activity, performance of works, want of tranquillity, desire,—these, O bull of Bharata's race, are born when passion is developed. [BG 14.13] Gloom, inactivity, error, and delusion also,—these, O son of Kuru's race, are born when darkness is developed. [BG 14.14] When the holder of a body goeth to dissolution while goodness is developed, then he attaineth to the spotless regions of those that know the Supreme. [BG 14.15] Going to dissolution when passion prevails, one is born among those that are attached to work. Likewise, dissolved during darkness, one is born in wombs that beget the ignorant. [BG 14.16] The fruit of good action is said to be good and untainted. The fruit, however, of passion, is misery; (and) the fruit of Darkness is ignorance. [BG 14.17] From goodness is produced knowledge; from passion, avarice; (and) from darkness are error and delusion, and also ignorance. [BG 14.18] They that dwell in goodness go on high; they that are addicted to passion dwell in the middle; (while) they that are of darkness, being addicted to the lowest quality, go down.

sections.title: Going beyond the three gunas
sections.label: BG 14.19-27
sections.text: [BG 14.19] When an observer recognises none else to be an agent save the qualities, and knows that which is beyond (the qualities), he attaineth to my nature. [BG 14.20] The embodied soul, by transcending these three qualities which constitute the source of all bodies, enjoyeth immortality, being freed from birth, death, decrepitude, and misery. [BG 14.21] What are indications, O Lord, of one who hath transcended these three qualities? What is his conduct? How also doth one transcend these three qualities? [BG 14.22] He who hath no aversion for light, activity, and even delusion, O son of Pandu, [BG 14.23] when they are present, nor desireth them when they are absent, who, seated as one unconcerned, is not shaken by those qualities; who sitteth and moveth not, [BG 14.24] thinking that it is the qualities (and not he) that are engaged (in their respective functions); to whom pain and pleasure are alike, who is self-contained, and to whom a sod of earth, [BG 14.25] a stone, and gold are alike; to whom the agreeable and the disagreeable are the same; who hath discernment; to whom censure and praise are the same; to whom honour and dishonour are the same; who regardeth friend and foe alike; who hath renounced all exertion—is said to have transcended the qualities. [BG 14.26] He also who worshippeth Me with exclusive devotion, he, transcending those qualities, becometh fit for admission into the nature of Brahma. [BG 14.27] For I am the stay of Brahma, of immortality, of undestructibility, of eternal piety, and of unbroken felicity.

sections.title: The inverted ashvattha tree of worldly life
sections.label: BG 15.1-6
sections.text: [BG 15.1] They say that the Aswattha, having its roots above and branches below, is eternal, its leaves are the Chhandas. He who knoweth it, knoweth the Vedas. [BG 15.2] Downwards and upwards are stretched its branches which are enlarged by the qualities; its sprouts are the objects of senses. [BG 15.3] Downwards its roots, leading to action, are extended to this world of men. Its form cannot here (below) be thus known, nor (its) end, nor (its) beginning, nor (its) support. [BG 15.4] Cutting, with the hard weapon of unconcern, this Aswattha of roots firmly fixed, then should one seek for that place repairing whither one returneth not again (thinking)—"I will seek the protection of that Primeval Sire from whom the ancient course of (worldly) life hath flowed."—Those that are free from pride and delusion, [BG 15.5] that have subdued the evil of attachment, that are steady in the contemplation of the relation of the Supreme to the individual self, from whom desire hath departed, freed from the pairs of opposites known by the names of pleasure and pain (and the like), repair, undeluded, to that eternal seat. [BG 15.6] The sun lighteth not that seat, nor the moon, nor fire. Whither going none returneth, that is my supreme seat.

sections.title: The soul as a fragment of Krishna
sections.label: BG 15.7-11
sections.text: [BG 15.7] An eternal portion of Me is that which, becoming an individual soul in the world of life, draweth to itself the (five) senses with the mind as the sixth which all depend on nature. [BG 15.8] When the sovereign (of this bodily frame) assumeth or quitteth (a) body, it departeth taking away these, like the wind (taking away) perfumes from their seats. [BG 15.9] Presiding over the ear, the eye, (the organs of) touch, taste, and smell, and also over the mind, he enjoyeth all objects of senses. [BG 15.10] They that are deluded do not see (him) when quitting or abiding in (the body), when enjoying or joined to the qualities. They (however) see that have the eye of knowledge. [BG 15.11] Devotees exerting (towards that end) behold him dwelling in themselves. They (however) that are senseless and whose minds are not restrained, behold him not, even while exerting (themselves).

sections.title: The divine light that sustains all
sections.label: BG 15.12-15
sections.text: [BG 15.12] That splendour dwelling in the sun which illumines the vast universe, that (which is) in the moon, and that (which is) in the fire, know that splendour to be mine. [BG 15.13] Entering into the earth I uphold creatures by my force; and becoming the juicy moon I nourish all herbs. [BG 15.14] Myself becoming the vital heat (Vaiswanara) residing in the bodies of creatures that breathe, (and) uniting with the upward and the downward life-breaths, I digest the four kinds of food. [BG 15.15] I am seated in the hearts of all. From Me are memory and knowledge and the loss of both. I am the objects of knowledge to be known by (the aid of) all the Vedas.

sections.title: The Supreme Person (Purushottama)
sections.label: BG 15.16-20
sections.text: [BG 15.16] I am the author of the Vedantas, and I alone am the knower of the Vedas. [BG 15.17] There are these two entities in the world, viz., the mutable and the immutable. The mutable is all (these) creatures. The unchangeable one is called the immutable. [BG 15.18] But there is another, the Supreme Being, called Paramatman, who was the Eternal Lord, pervading the three worlds, sustaineth (them) (and) since I transcend the mutable, and am higher than even the immutable; for this I am celebrated in the world (among men) and in the Veda as Purushottama (the Highest Being). [BG 15.19] He who, without being deluded, knoweth Me as this Highest Being,—he knowing all, O Bharata, worshippeth Me in every way. [BG 15.20] Thus, O sinless one, hath this knowledge, forming the greatest of mysteries, been declared by Me (to thee). Knowing this, O Bharata, one will become gifted with intelligence, and will have done all he needs do.

sections.title: The divine qualities
sections.label: BG 16.1-5
sections.text: [BG 16.1] Fearlessness, purity of heart, perseverance in (the pursuit of) knowledge and Yoga meditation, gifts, self-restraint, sacrifice, study of the Vedas, [BG 16.2] ascetic penances, uprightness, abstention from injury, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquillity, freedom from reporting other's faults, compassion for all creatures, absence of covetousness, [BG 16.3] gentleness, modesty, absence of restlessness, vigour, forgiveness, firmness, cleanliness, absence of quarrelsomeness, freedom from vanity,—these become his, O Bharata, who is born to godlike possessions. [BG 16.4] Hypocrisy, pride, conceit, wrath, rudeness and ignorance, are, O son of Pritha, his who is born to demoniac possessions. [BG 16.5] God-like possessions are deemed to be for deliverance; the demoniac for bondage. Grieve not, O son of Pandu, for thou art born to god-like possessions.

sections.title: The demonic nature
sections.label: BG 16.6-20
sections.text: [BG 16.6] (There are) two kinds of created beings in this world, viz., the god-like and the demoniac. The god-like have been described at length. Hear now, from me, O son of Pritha, about the demoniac. [BG 16.7] Persons of demoniac nature know not inclination or disinclination. Neither purity, nor good conduct, nor truth exist in them. [BG 16.8] They say that the universe is void of truth, of guiding principle, (and) of ruler; produced by the union of one another (male and female) from lust, and nothing else. [BG 16.9] Depending on this view, these men of lost selves, little intelligence, and fierce deeds, these enemies (of the world), are born for the destruction of the universe. [BG 16.10] Cherishing desires that are insatiable, and endued with hypocrisy, conceit and folly, they adopt false notions through delusion and engage in unholy practices. [BG 16.11] Cherishing boundless thoughts limited by death (alone), and regarding the enjoyment of (their) desires as the highest end, they are persuaded that that is all. [BG 16.12] Fettered by the hundred nooses of hope, addicted to lust and wrath, they covet to obtain this wealth to-day, [BG 16.13] This I will obtain later,—This wealth I have,—This (wealth) will be mine in addition,—This foe hath been slain by me, [BG 16.14] I will slay even others,—I am lord,—I am the enjoyer,—I am successful, powerful, happy,—I am rich and of noble birth, [BG 16.15] Who else is there that is like me?—I will sacrifice,—I will make gifts,—I will be merry, [BG 16.16] thus deluded by ignorance, tossed about by numerous thoughts, enveloped in the meshes of delusion, attached to the enjoyment of objects of desire, they sink into foul hell. [BG 16.17] Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices that are nominally so, with hypocrisy and against the (prescribed) ordinance. [BG 16.18] Wedded to vanity, power, pride, lust and wrath, these revilers hate Me in their own bodies and those of others. [BG 16.19] These haters (of Me), cruel, the vilest among men, and unholy, I hurl continually down into demoniac wombs. [BG 16.20] Coming into demoniac wombs, deluded birth after birth, they, O son of Kunti, without attaining to Me go down to the vilest state.

sections.title: Lust, anger, greed: the gates of hell
sections.label: BG 16.21-24
sections.text: [BG 16.21] Three-fold is the way to hell, ruinous to the self, viz., lust, wrath, likewise avarice. Therefore, these three, one should renounce. [BG 16.22] Freed from these three gates of darkness, a man, O son of Kunti, works out his own welfare, and then repairs to his highest goal. [BG 16.23] He who, abandoning the ordinances of the scriptures, acts only under the impulses of desire, never attains to perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal. [BG 16.24] Therefore, the scriptures should be thy authority in determining what should be done and what should not be done. It behoveth thee to do work here, having ascertained what hath been declared by the ordinances of the scriptures.

sections.title: Three kinds of faith
sections.label: BG 17.1-6
sections.text: [BG 17.1] What is the state, O Krishna, of those who abandoning the ordinance of the scriptures, perform sacrifices endued with faith? It is one of Goodness, or Passion, or Darkness? [BG 17.2] The faith of embodied (creatures) is of three kinds. It is (also) born of their (individual) natures. It is good, passionate, and dark. Hear now these. [BG 17.3] The faith of one, O Bharata, is conformable to his own nature. A being here is full of faith; and whatever is one's faith, one is even that. [BG 17.4] They that are of the quality of goodness worship the gods; they that are of the quality of passion (worship) the Yakshas and the Rakshasas; other people that are of the quality of darkness worship departed spirits and hosts of Bhutas. [BG 17.5] Those people who practise severe ascetic austerities not ordained by the scriptures, are given up to hypocrisy and pride, and endued with desire of attachment, and violence, [BG 17.6] those persons possessed of no discernment, torturing the groups of organs in (their) bodies and Me also seated within (those) bodies,—should be known to be of demoniac resolves.

sections.title: Three kinds of food
sections.label: BG 17.7-10
sections.text: [BG 17.7] Food which is dear to all is of three kinds. Sacrifice, penance, and gifts are likewise (of three kinds). Listen to their distinctions as follows. [BG 17.8] Those kinds of food that increase life's period, energy, strength, health, well-being, and joy, which are savoury, oleaginous, nutritive, and agreeable, are liked by God. [BG 17.9] Those kinds of food which are bitter, sour, salted, over-hot, pungent, dry, and burning, and which produce pain, grief and disease, are desired by the passionate. [BG 17.10] The food which is cold, without savour, stinking and corrupt, and which is even refuse, and filthy, is dear to men of darkness.

sections.title: Sacrifice, austerity and charity by the gunas
sections.label: BG 17.11-22
sections.text: [BG 17.11] That sacrifice is good which, being prescribed by the ordinance, is performed by persons, without any longing for the fruit (thereof) and the mind being determined (to it under the belief) that its performance is a duty. [BG 17.12] But that which is performed in expectation of fruit and even for the sake of ostentation, know that sacrifice, O chief of the sons of Bharata, to be of the quality of passion. [BG 17.13] That sacrifice which is against the ordinance, in which no food is dealt out, which is devoid of mantras (sacred verse), in which no fees are paid to the brahmanas assisting to it, and which is void of faith, is said to be of the quality of darkness. [BG 17.14] Reverence to the gods, regenerate ones, preceptors, and men of knowledge, purity, uprightness, the practices of a Brahmacharin, and abstention from injury, are said to constitute the penance of the body. [BG 17.15] The speech which causeth no agitation, which is true, which is agreeable and beneficial, and the diligent study of the Vedas, are said to be the penance of speech. [BG 17.16] Serenity of the mind, gentleness, taciturnity, self-restraint, and purity of the disposition,—these are said to be the penance of the mind. [BG 17.17] This three-fold penance performed with perfect faith, by men without desire of fruit, and with devotion, is said to be of the quality of goodness. [BG 17.18] That penance which is performed for the sake of (gaining) respect, honour, and reverence, with hypocrisy, (and) which is unstable and transient is said to be of the quality of passion. [BG 17.19] That penance which is performed under a deluded conviction, with torture of one's self, and for the destruction of another, is said to be of the quality of darkness. [BG 17.20] That gift which is given because it ought to be given, to one who cannot return any service for it, in a proper time, and to a proper person, is said to be of the quality of goodness. [BG 17.21] That, however, which is given reluctantly, for return of services (past or expected), or even with an eye to fruit,—that gift is said to be of the quality of passion. [BG 17.22] In an unfit place and at an unfit time, the gift that is made to an unworthy object, without respect, and with contempt, is said to be of the quality of darkness.

sections.title: Om Tat Sat
sections.label: BG 17.23-28
sections.text: [BG 17.23] OM, TAT, SAT, this is said to be the three-fold designation of Brahma. By that (Brahma), the Brahmanas and the Vedas, and the Sacrifices, were ordained of old. [BG 17.24] Therefore, uttering the syllable OM, the sacrifices, gifts, and penances, prescribed by the ordinance, of all utterers of Brahma begin. [BG 17.25] Uttering TAT, the various rites of sacrifice, penance, and gifts, without expectation of fruit, are performed by those that are desirous of deliverance. [BG 17.26] SAT is employed to denote existence and goodness. Likewise, O son of Pritha, the word SAT is used in any auspicious act. [BG 17.27] Constancy in sacrifices, in penances and in gifts, is also called SAT, and an act, too, for the sake of That is called SAT. [BG 17.28] Whatever oblation is offered (to the fire), whatever is given away, whatever penance is performed, whatever is done, without faith, is, O son of Pritha, said to be the opposite of SAT; and that is nought both here and hereafter.

sections.title: Sannyasa and tyaga: renounce the fruits
sections.label: BG 18.1-12
sections.text: [BG 18.1] Of renunciation, O thou of mighty arms, I desire to know the true nature, and also of abandonment, O lord of the senses distinctly, O slayer of Kesi. [BG 18.2] The rejection of the works with desire is known by the learned as renunciation. The abandonment of the fruit of all work, the discerning call abandonment. [BG 18.3] Some wise men say that work (itself) should be abandoned as evil; others (say) that the works of sacrifice, gifts, and penance, should not be abandoned. [BG 18.4] As to that abandonment, listen to my decision, O best of the sons of Bharata, for abandonment, O tiger among men, hath been declared to be of three kinds. [BG 18.5] The works of sacrifice, gifts, and penance should not be abandoned. They should, indeed, be done. Sacrifice, gift, and penance, are the purifications of the wise. [BG 18.6] But even those works should be done, abandoning attachment and fruit. This, O son of Pritha, is my excellent and decided opinion. [BG 18.7] The renunciation of an act prescribed (in the scriptures) is not proper. Its abandonment (is) from delusion, (and) is (therefore,) declared to be of the quality of darkness. [BG 18.8] (Regarding it) as (a source of) sorrow, when work is abandoned from (fear of) bodily pain, one making such an abandonment which is of the quality of passion never obtaineth the fruit of abandonment. [BG 18.9] (Regarding it) as one that should be done, when work that is prescribed (in the scriptures) is done, O Arjuna, abandoning attachment and fruit also, that abandonment is deemed to be of the quality of goodness. [BG 18.10] Possessed of intelligence and with doubts dispelled, an abandoner that is endowed with the quality of goodness hath no aversion for an unpleasant action and no attachment to pleasant (ones). [BG 18.11] Since actions cannot be absolutely abandoned by an embodied person, (therefore) he who abandons the fruit of actions is truly said to be an abandoner. [BG 18.12] Evil, good and mixed-action hath (this) three-fold fruit hereafter for those that do not abandon. But there is none whatever for the renouncer.

sections.title: The five causes of every action
sections.label: BG 18.13-18
sections.text: [BG 18.13] Listen from me, O thou of mighty arms, to those five causes for the completion of all actions, declared in the Sankhya treating of the annihilation of actions. [BG 18.14] (They are) substratum, agent, the diverse kinds of organs, the diverse efforts severally, and with them the deities as the fifth. [BG 18.15] With body, speech, or mind, whatever work, just or the reverse, a man undertakes, these five are its causes. [BG 18.16] That being so, he that, owing to an unrefined understanding, beholdeth his own self as solely the agent, he, dull in mind, beholdeth not. [BG 18.17] He that hath no feeling of egoism, whose mind is not sullied, he, even killing all these people, killeth not, nor is fettered (by action).—Knowledge, [BG 18.18] the object of knowledge, and the knower, form the three-fold impulse of action. Instrument, action, and the agent, form the three-fold complement of action.

sections.title: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect and happiness by the gunas
sections.label: BG 18.19-40
sections.text: [BG 18.19] Knowledge, action, and agent, are declared in the enumeration of qualities to be three-fold, according to the difference of qualities. Listen to those also duly. [BG 18.20] That by which One Eternal Essence is viewed in all things, undivided in the divided, know that to be knowledge having the quality of goodness. [BG 18.21] That knowledge which discerneth all things as diverse essences of different kinds in consequence of their separateness, know that that knowledge hath the quality of passion. [BG 18.22] But that which is attached to (each) single object as if it were the whole, which is without reason, without truth, and mean, that knowledge hath been said to be of the quality of darkness. [BG 18.23] The action which is prescribed (by the scriptures), (done) without attachment, performed without desires and aversion, by one who longeth not for (its) fruit, is said to be of the quality of goodness. [BG 18.24] But that action which is done by one seeking objects of desire, or by one filled with egoism, and which is attended with great trouble, is said to be of the quality of passion. [BG 18.25] That action which is undertaken from delusion, without regard to consequences, loss, injury (to others), and (one's own) power also, is said to be of the quality of passion. [BG 18.26] The agent who is free from attachment, who never speaketh of himself, who is endued with constancy and energy, and is unmoved by success and defeat, is said to be of the quality of goodness. [BG 18.27] The agent who is full of affections, who wisheth for the fruit of actions, who is covetous, endued with cruelty, and impure, and who feeleth joy and sorrow, is declared to be of the quality of passion. [BG 18.28] The agent who is void of application, without discernment, obstinate, deceitful, malicious, slothful, desponding, and procrastinating, is said to be of the quality of darkness. [BG 18.29] Hear now, O Dhananjaya, the three-fold division of intellect and constancy, according to their qualities, which I am about to declare exhaustively and distinctly. [BG 18.30] The intellect which knoweth action and inaction, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and deliverance, is, O son of Pritha, of the quality of goodness. [BG 18.31] The intellect by which one imperfectly discerneth right and wrong, that which ought to be done and that which ought not to be done, is, O son of Pritha, of the quality of passion. [BG 18.32] That intellect which, shrouded by darkness, regardeth wrong to be right, and all things as reversed, is, O son of Pritha, of the quality of darkness. [BG 18.33] That unswerving constancy by which one controls the functions of the mind, the life-breaths, and the senses, through devotion, that constancy, is, O son of Pritha, of the quality of goodness. [BG 18.34] But that constancy, O Arjuna, by which one holds to religion, desire, and profit, through attachment, desiring fruit, that constancy, O son of Pritha, is of the quality of passion. [BG 18.35] That through which an undiscerning person abandons not sleep, fear, sorrow, despondency, and folly, that constancy is deemed to be of the quality of darkness. [BG 18.36] Hear now from me, O bull of Bharata's race, of the three kinds of happiness. That in which one findeth pleasure from repetition (of enjoyment), which bringeth an end to pain, which is like poison first but resembleth nectar in the end, [BG 18.37] that happiness born of the serenity produced by a knowledge of self, is said to be of the quality of goodness. [BG 18.38] That which is from the contact of the senses with their objects which resembleth nectar first but is like poison in the end, that happiness is held to be of the quality of passion. [BG 18.39] That happiness which in the beginning and its consequences deludeth the soul, and springeth from sleep, indolence, and stupidity, that is described to be of the quality of darkness. [BG 18.40] There is not, either on earth or heaven among the gods, the entity that is free from these three qualities born of nature.

sections.title: Duty born of one's own nature
sections.label: BG 18.41-48
sections.text: [BG 18.41] The duties of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaisyas, and of Sudras also, O chastiser of foes, are distinguished by (these three) qualities born of nature. [BG 18.42] Tranquillity, self-restraint, ascetic austerities, purity, forgiveness, rectitude, knowledge, experience, and belief (in an existence hereafter),—these are the duties of Brahmanas, born of (their proper) nature. [BG 18.43] Bravery, energy, firmness, skill, not flying away from battle, liberality, the bearing of a ruler,—these are the duties of Kshatriyas, born of (their proper) nature. [BG 18.44] Agriculture, tending of cattle, and trade, are the natural duties of Vaisyas. Of Sudras also, the natural duty consists in servitude. [BG 18.45] Every man, engaged in his own duties, attains to perfection. Hear now how one obtains perfection by application to his duties. [BG 18.46] Him from whom are the movements of all beings, Him by whom all this is pervaded, worshipping him by (the performance of) one's own duty, one obtaineth perfection. [BG 18.47] Better is one's own duty though performed faultily than another's duty well-performed. Performing the duty prescribed by (one's own) nature, one incurreth no sin. [BG 18.48] One must not abandon, O son of Kunti, one's natural duty though tainted with evil, for all actions are enveloped by evil like fire by smoke.

sections.title: Perfection and the attainment of Brahman
sections.label: BG 18.49-60
sections.text: [BG 18.49] He whose mind is unattached everywhere, who hath subdued his self, and whose desire hath departed, obtaineth, through renunciation, the supreme perfection of freedom from work. [BG 18.50] Learn from me, only in brief, O son of Kunti, how one, having obtained (this kind of) perfection, attaineth to Brahma which is the supreme end of knowledge. [BG 18.51] Endued with a pure mind, and restraining his self by constancy, renouncing sound and other objects of sense, and casting off affection and aversion, he who resideth in a lonely place, [BG 18.52] eateth little, and restraineth speech, body, and mind, who is ever intent on meditation and abstraction, who hath recourse to indifference, who, abandoning egoism, [BG 18.53] violence, pride, lust, wrath, and (all) surroundings, hath been freed from selfishness and is tranquil (in mind), becometh fit for assimilation with Brahma. [BG 18.54] Becoming one with Brahma, tranquil in spirit, (such a) one grieveth not, desireth not; alike to all beings, he obtaineth the highest devotion to Me. [BG 18.55] By (that) devotion he truly understandeth Me. What I am, and who I am; then understanding Me truly, he entereth into Me forthwith. [BG 18.56] Even performing all actions at all times having refuge in Me, he obtaineth, through my favour, the seat that is eternal and imperishable. [BG 18.57] Dedicating in thy heart all actions to Me, being devoted to Me, resorting to mental abstraction, fix thy thoughts constantly on Me. [BG 18.58] Fixing thy thoughts on Me, thou wilt surmount all difficulties through my grace. But if from self-conceit thou wilt not listen, thou wilt (then) utterly perish. [BG 18.59] If, having recourse to self-conceit, thou thinkest—I will not fight,—that resolution of thine would be vain, (for) Nature will constrain thee. [BG 18.60] That which, from delusion, thou dost not wish to do, thou wilt do involuntarily, bound by thy own duty springing from (thy own) nature.

sections.title: The supreme secret: take refuge in Krishna
sections.label: BG 18.61-66
sections.text: [BG 18.61] The Lord, O Arjuna, dwelleth in the region of the heart of beings, turning all beings as if mounted on a machine, by his illusive power. [BG 18.62] Seek shelter with Him in every way, O Bharata. Through his grace thou wilt obtain supreme tranquillity, the eternal seat. [BG 18.63] Thus hath been declared to thee by Me the knowledge that is more mysterious than any (other) matter. Reflecting on it fully, act as thou likest. [BG 18.64] Once more, listen to my supernal words, the most mysterious of all. Exceedingly dear art thou to Me, therefore, I will declare what is for thy benefit. [BG 18.65] Set thy heart on Me, become My devotee, sacrifice to Me, bow down to Me. Then shalt thou come to Me. I declare to thee truly, (for) thou art dear to Me. [BG 18.66] Forsaking all (religious) duties, come to Me as thy sole refuge. I will deliver thee from all sins. Do not grieve.

sections.title: The glory of the teaching; Arjuna's doubts dispelled
sections.label: BG 18.67-73
sections.text: [BG 18.67] This is not to be ever declared by thee to one who practiseth no austerities, to one who is not a devotee, to one who never waiteth on a preceptor, nor yet to one who calumniateth Me. [BG 18.68] He who shall inculcate this supreme mystery to those that are devoted to Me, offering Me the highest devotion, will come to Me, freed from (all his) doubts. [BG 18.69] Amongst men there is none who can do Me a dearer service than he, nor shall any other on earth be dearer to Me than he. [BG 18.70] And he who will study this holy converse between us, by him will have been offered to Me the sacrifice of knowledge. Such is my opinion. [BG 18.71] Even the man who, with faith and without cavil, will hear it (read), even he freed (from re-birth), will obtain of the blessed regions of those that perform pious acts. [BG 18.72] Hath this, O son of Pritha, been heard by thee with mind undirected to any other objects? Hath thy delusion, (caused) by ignorance, been destroyed, O Dhananjaya? [BG 18.73] My delusion hath been destroyed, and the recollection (of what I am) hath been gained by me, O Undeteriorating one, through thy favour. I am now firm. My doubts have been dispelled. I will do thy bidding.

sections.title: Sanjaya's closing words
sections.label: BG 18.74-78
sections.text: [BG 18.74] Thus I heard this converse between Vasudeva and the high-souled son of Pritha, (that is) wonderful and causeth the hair to stand on end. [BG 18.75] Through Vyasa's favour heard I this supreme mystery, this (doctrine of) Yoga, from Krishna himself, the Lord of Yoga, who declared it in person. [BG 18.76] O King recollecting and (again) recollecting this wonderful (and) holy converse of Kesava and Arjuna, I rejoice over and over again. [BG 18.77] Recollecting again and again that wonderful form also of Hari, great is my amazement, O king, and I rejoice ever more. [BG 18.78] Thither where Krishna, the Lord of Yoga (is), thither where the great bowman (Partha) is, thither, in my opinion, are prosperity, and victory, and greatness, and eternal justice

verses.speaker: Dhritarashtra
verses.sanskrit_iast: dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ | māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kim akurvata saṃjaya
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किम्अकुर्वत संजय ॥
verses.english: Assembled together on the sacred plain of Kurukshetra from desire of fighting what did my sons and the Pandavas do, O Sanjaya.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanas tadā | ācāryam upasaṃgamya rājā vacanam abravīt
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा । आचार्यम्उपसंगम्य राजा वचनम्अब्रवीत् ॥
verses.english: Beholding the army of the Pandavas arrayed, king Duryodhana, approaching the preceptor (Drona) said these words:

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇām ācārya mahatīṃ camūm | vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणाम्आचार्य महतीं चमूम् । व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥
verses.english: Behold, O preceptor, this vast army of the son of Pandu, arrayed by Drupada's son (Dhrishtadyumna), thy intelligent disciple.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi | yuyudhāno virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि । युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥
verses.english: There (in that army) are many brave and mighty bowmen, who in battle are equal to Bhima and Arjuna.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: dhṛṣṭaketuś cekitānaḥ kāśirājaś ca vīryavān | purujit kuntibhojaś ca śaibyaś ca narapuṃgavaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् । पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुंगवः ॥
verses.english: (They are) Yuyudhana, and Virata, and that mighty car-warrior Drupada, and Dhrishtaketu, and Chekitana, and the ruler of Kasi endued with great energy; and Purujit,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: yudhāmanyuś ca vikrānta uttamaujāś ca vīryavān | saubhadro draupadeyāś ca sarva eva mahārathāḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् । सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥
verses.english: and Kuntibhoja, and Saivya that bull among men; and Yudhamanyu of great prowess, and Uttamaujas of great energy; and Subhadra's son, and the sons of Draupadi, all of whom are mighty car-warriors.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tān nibodha dvijottama | nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tān bravīmi te
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम । नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
verses.english: Hear, however, O best of regenerate ones, who are the distinguished ones among us, the leaders of the army. I will name them to thee for (thy) information.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: bhavān bhīṣmaś ca karṇaś ca kṛpaś ca samitiṃjayaḥ | aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca saumadattir jayadrathaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिंजयः । अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिर्जयद्रथः ॥
verses.english: (They are) thyself, and Bhishma, and Karna, and Kripa who is ever victorious; and Aswatthaman and Vikarna, and Saumadatta, and Jayadratha.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ | nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः । नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥
verses.english: Besides these, are many heroic warriors, prepared to lay down their lives for my sake, armed with diverse kinds of weapons, and all accomplished in battle.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: aparyāptaṃ tad asmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam | paryāptaṃ tv idam eteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अपर्याप्तं तद्अस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् । पर्याप्तं त्व्इदम्एतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥
verses.english: Our army, therefore, protected by Bhishma, is insufficient. This force, however, of these (the Pandavas), protected by Bhima, is sufficient.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgam avasthitāḥ | bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागम्अवस्थिताः । भीष्मम्एवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥
verses.english: Stationing yourselves then in the entrances of the divisions that have been assigned to you, all of you protect Bhishma alone.'—(Just at this time) the valiant and venerable grandsire of the Kurus,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: tasya saṃjanayan harṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ | siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः । सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥
verses.english: affording great joy to him (Duryodhana) by loudly uttering a leonine roar, blew (his) conch.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ | sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः । सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलो ऽभवत् ॥
verses.english: Then conches and drums and cymbals and horns were sounded at once and the noise (made) became a loud uproar.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau | mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaś caiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ । माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥
verses.english: Then Madhava and Pandu's son (Arjuna), both stationed on a great car unto which were yoked white steeds, blew their celestial conches.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ | pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनंजयः । पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥
verses.english: And Hrishikesa blew (the conch called) Panchajanya and Dhananjaya (that called) Devadatta; and Vrikodara of terrible deeds blew the huge conch (called) Paundra.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ | nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥
verses.english: And Kunti's son king Yudhishthira blew (the conch called) Anantavijaya; while Nakula and Sahadeva, (those conches called respectively) Sughosa and Manipushpaka.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: kāśyaś ca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ | dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś cāparājitaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः । धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥
verses.english: And that splendid bowman, the ruler of Kasi and that mighty car-warrior, Sikhandin, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and that unvanquished Satyaki,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: drupado draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate | saubhadraś ca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते । सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
verses.english: and Drupada, and the sons of Draupadi, and the mighty-armed son of Subhadra—all these, O lord of earth, severally blew their conches.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat | nabhaś ca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् । नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥
verses.english: And that blare, loudly reverberating through the welkin, and the earth, rent the hearts of the Dhartarashtras.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasaṃpāte dhanur udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः । प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुर्उद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥
verses.english: Then beholding the Dhartarashtra troops drawn up, the ape-bannered son of Pandu, rising his bow,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyam idam āha mahīpate | senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me 'cyuta
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यम्इदम्आह महीपते । सेनयोर्उभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मे ऽच्युत ॥
verses.english: when, the throwing of missiles had just commenced, said these words, O lord of earth, to Hrishikesa.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: yāvad etān nirīkṣe 'haṃ yoddhukāmān avasthitān | kair mayā saha yoddhavyam asmin raṇasamudyame
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: यावद्एतान्निरीक्षे ऽहं योद्धुकामान्अवस्थितान् । कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यम्अस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ॥
verses.english: O thou that knoweth no deterioration, place my car (once) between the two armies, so that I may observe these that stand here desirous of battle, and with whom I shall have to contend in the labours of this struggle.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: yotsyamānān avekṣe 'haṃ ya ete 'tra samāgatāḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddher yuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: योत्स्यमानान्अवेक्षे ऽहं य एते ऽत्र समागताः । धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥
verses.english: I will observe those who are assembled here and who are prepared to fight for doing what is agreeable in battle to the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: evam ukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata | senayor ubhayor madhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: एवम्उक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत । सेनयोर्उभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by Gudakesa, O Bharata, Hrishikesa, placing that excellent car between the two armies,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām | uvāca pārtha paśyaitān samavetān kurūn iti
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् । उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरून्इति ॥
verses.english: in view of Bhishma and Drona and all the kings of the earth, said,—'Behold, O Partha these assembled Kurus,'—And there the son of Pritha beheld,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: tatrāpaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṝn atha pitāmahān | ācāryān mātulān bhrātṝn putrān pautrān sakhīṃs tathā
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄन्अथ पितामहान् । आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥
verses.english: standing (his) sires and grandsons, and friends, and father-in-law and well-wishers, in both the armies.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: śvaśurān suhṛdaś caiva senayor ubhayor api | tān samīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोर्उभयोर्अपि । तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धून्अवस्थितान् ॥
verses.english: Beholding all those kinsmen standing (there), the son of Kunti, possessed by excessive pity, despondingly said (these words).

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdann idam abravīt | dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्न्इदम्अब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
verses.english: Beholding these kinsmen, O Krishna, assembled together and eager for the fight, my limbs become languid, and my mouth becomes dry.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati | vepathuś ca śarīre me romaharṣaś ca jāyate
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥
verses.english: My body trembles, and my hair stands on end. Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāt tvak caiva paridahyate | na ca śaknomy avasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्य्अवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
verses.english: I am unable to stand (any longer); my mind seems to wander.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava | na ca śreyo 'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanam āhave
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव । न च श्रेयो ऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनम्आहवे ॥
verses.english: I behold adverse omens, too, O Kesava. I do not desire victory, O Krishna, not sovereignty, nor pleasures.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca | kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogair jīvitena vā
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च । किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
verses.english: Of what use would sovereignty be to us, O Govinda, or enjoyments, or even life, since they, for whose sake sovereignty, enjoyments,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: yeṣām arthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca | ta ime 'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃs tyaktvā dhanāni ca
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: येषाम्अर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च । त इमे ऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
verses.english: and pleasures are desired by us, are here arrayed for battle ready to give up life and wealth,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ | mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ saṃbandhinas tathā
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः । मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः संबन्धिनस्तथा ॥
verses.english: viz., preceptors, sires, sons and grandsires, maternal uncles, father-in-laws, grandsons, brother-in-laws, and kinsmen.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: etān na hantum icchāmi ghnato 'pi madhusūdana | api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: एतान्न हन्तुम्इच्छामि घ्नतो ऽपि मधुसूदन । अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
verses.english: I wish not to slay these though they slay me, O slayer of Madhu, even for the sake of the sovereignty of the three worlds, what then for the sake of (this) earth?

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana | pāpam evāśrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन । पापम्एवाश्रयेद्अस्मान्हत्वैतान्आततायिनः ॥
verses.english: What gratification can be ours, O Janardana, by slaying the Dhartarashtras? Even if they be regarded as foes, sin will overtake us if we slay them.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: tasmān nārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrān svabāndhavān | svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् । स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
verses.english: Therefore, it behoveth us not to slay the sons of Dhritarashtra who are our own kinsmen. How, O Madhava can we be happy by killing our own kinsmen?

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: yady apy ete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ | kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: यद्य्अप्य्एते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥
verses.english: Even if these, with judgments perverted by avarice, do not see the evil that ariseth from the extermination of a race,

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: kathaṃ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum | kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhir janārdana
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: कथं न ज्ञेयम्अस्माभिः पापाद्अस्मान्निवर्तितुम् । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥
verses.english: and the sin of internecine quarrels, why should not we, O Janardana, who see the evils of the extermination of a race, learn to abstain from that sin?

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ | dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnam adharmo 'bhibhavaty uta
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः । धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नम्अधर्मो ऽभिभवत्य्उत ॥
verses.english: A race being destroyed, the eternal customs of that race are lost; and upon those customs being lost, sin overpowers the whole race.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ | strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः । स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसंकरः ॥
verses.english: From the predominance of sin, O Krishna, the women of that race become corrupt. And the women becoming corrupt, an intermingling of castes happeneth, O descendant of Vrishni.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: saṃkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca | patanti pitaro hy eṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: संकरो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च । पतन्ति पितरो ह्य्एषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥
verses.english: This intermingling of castes leadeth to hell both the destroyer of the race and the race itself. The ancestors of those fall (from heaven), their rites of pinda and water ceasing.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: doṣair etaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṃkarakārakaiḥ | utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāś ca śāśvatāḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: दोषैर्एतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसंकरकारकैः । उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥
verses.english: By these sins of destroyers of races, causing intermixture of castes, the rules of caste and the eternal rites of families become extinct.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana | narake niyataṃ vāso bhavatīty anuśuśruma
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन । नरके नियतं वासो भवतीत्य्अनुशुश्रुम ॥
verses.english: We have heard, O Janardana, that men whose family rites become extinct, ever dwell in hell.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: aho bata mahat pāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam | yad rājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ svajanam udyatāḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् । यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनम्उद्यताः ॥
verses.english: Alas, we have resolved to perpetrate a great sin, for we are ready to slay our own kinsmen from lust of the sweets of sovereignty.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṃ bhavet
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: यदि माम्अप्रतीकारम्अशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः । धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥
verses.english: Better would it be for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapon in hand, should in battle slay me (myself) unavenging unarmed.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: evam uktvārjunaḥ saṃkhye rathopastha upāviśat | visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: एवम्उक्त्वार्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
verses.english: Having spoken thus on the field of battle, Arjuna, his mind troubled with grief, casting aside his bow and arrows, sat down on his car.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam | viṣīdantam idaṃ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: तं तथा कृपयाविष्टम्अश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् । विषीदन्तम्इदं वाक्यम्उवाच मधुसूदनः ॥
verses.english: Unto him thus possessed with pity, his eyes filled and oppressed with tears, and desponding, the slayer of Madhu said these words.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.sanskrit_iast: kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṃ viṣame samupasthitam | anāryajuṣṭam asvargyam akīrtikaram arjuna
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: कुतस्त्वा कश्मलम्इदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टम्अस्वर्ग्यम्अकीर्तिकरम्अर्जुन ॥
verses.english: Whence, O Arjuna, hath come upon thee, at such a crisis, this despondency that is unbecoming a person of noble birth, that shuts one out from heaven, and that is productive of infamy?

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.sanskrit_iast: klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate | kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha paraṃtapa
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्य्उपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परंतप ॥
verses.english: Let no effeminacy be thine, O son of Kunti. This suits thee not. Shaking off this vile weakness of hearts, arise, O chastiser of foes.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit_iast: kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana | iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāv arisūdana
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: कथं भीष्मम्अहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन । इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हाव्अरिसूदन ॥
verses.english: How, O slayer of Madhu, can I with arrows contend in battle against Bhishma and Drona, deserving as they are, O slayer of foes, of worship?

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit_iast: gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvāñ | śreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣyam apīha loke | hatvārthakāmāṃs tu gurūn ihaiva | bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: गुरून्अहत्वा हि महानुभावाञ् । श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यम्अपीह लोके । हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरून्इहैव । भुञ्जीय भोगान्रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥
verses.english: Without slaying (one's) preceptors of great glory, it is well (for one), to live on even alms in this world. By slaying preceptors, even if they are avaricious of wealth, I should only enjoy pleasures that are bloodstained!

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit_iast: na caitad vidmaḥ kataran no garīyo | yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ | yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmas | te 'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो । यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यान्एव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस् । ते ऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
verses.english: We know not which of the two is of greater moment to us, viz., whether we should conquer them or they should conquer us. By slaying whom we would not like to live,—even they, the sons of Dhritarashtra, stand before (us).

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit_iast: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ | pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharmasaṃmūḍhacetāḥ | yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṃ brūhi tan me | śiṣyas te 'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः । पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे । शिष्यस्ते ऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
verses.english: My nature affected by the taint of compassion, my mind unsettled about (my) duty, I ask thee. Tell me what is assuredly good (for me). I am thy disciple. O, instruct me, I seek thy aid.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.sanskrit_iast: na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād | yac chokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām | avāpya bhūmāv asapatnam ṛddhaṃ | rājyaṃ surāṇām api cādhipatyam
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद् । यच्छोकम्उच्छोषणम्इन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमाव्असपत्नम्ऋद्धं । राज्यं सुराणाम्अपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
verses.english: I do not see (that) which would dispel that grief of mine blasting my very senses, even if I obtain a prosperous kingdom on earth without a foe or the very sovereignty of the gods.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ paraṃtapaḥ | na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: एवम्उक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परंतपः । न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दम्उक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
verses.english: Having said this unto Hrishikesa, that chastiser of foes—Gudakesa—(once more) addressed Govinda, saying,—'I will not fight,'—and then remained silent.

verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.sanskrit_iast: tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata | senayor ubhayor madhye viṣīdantam idaṃ vacaḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: तम्उवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्न्इव भारत । सेनयोर्उभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तम्इदं वचः ॥
verses.english: Unto him overcome by despondency, Hrishikesa, in the midst of the two armies, said:

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.sanskrit_iast: aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṃ prajñāvādāṃś ca bhāṣase | gatāsūn agatāsūṃś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: अशोच्यान्अन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे । गतासून्अगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
verses.english: Thou mournest those that deserve not to be mourned. Thou speakest also the words of the (so-called) wise. Those, however, that are (really) wise, grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.sanskrit_iast: na tv evāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ | na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param
verses.sanskrit_devanagari: न त्व्एवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयम्अतः परम् ॥
verses.english: It is not that. I or you or those rulers of men never were, or that all of us shall not hereafter be.
